main_text.p: fmeere. Sed & mpze lutum ex eodem fonte ; cum τὸ μύεγμα, ex quo μύεγν ortum, flere, fluere, fundere, in genere significet, & ista vulgò confundantur. Αλείφὶν, ungere, & illinere: ἀλοιφὴ, unguentum, & tectorium, quo parietes illinantur. Ita & Latina, venenum, inficere, in utramque partem usurpantur ; & alia plurima.
Μυσάω, nimio humore & uligine vitior; præ nimio humore seu madore putrefco : μύσηοις, vitium quod ex nimio humore & madore contrahitur ; mud, muft ; mudd̃p, mustp.
Μέλδω, liquefacio : Item macero, confumo, &c. to melt : Item, to moul-der.
Μῶλ@-, πόλεμ@-, μάχη, σύρυβ@-, μόλ@-, bellum, pugna, turba, labor ; Angl. to mople : vulgò jungunt, cum tolle, (to motle and toile) de quo vide in ἔταλ@-.
Μιγνύω, mifcere ; to mingle : μίγμα, mixtio ; a mixmalh.
Μαεγίνω, tabefacio ; μαεγνης, vel μαεγμός, tabes ; moraine, vel morrein : lues, tabifica lues: inter pecora proprie.

page.notes: Old English words are printed in black letter and italic within the roman text; Greek is printed as reproduced and may contain errors. The last line is partly cut off at the foot of the page.
